newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha gains ground on firmer crudes.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha gains ground on firmer crudes.

text.p: Tokyo naphtha prices firmed in afternoon trade on Thursday, following overnight gains in crude, market participants said.
Near-term naphtha spreads remained in contango, with second-half July/second-half August indicated at minus $1.50/minus $1.00.
First-half August open-spec naphtha was quoted at $216.50/$217.50 per tonne, compared with late Wednesday's $215.25/215.75.
Bids for second-half July were heard at $215.50, while offers were notionally assessed at $216.50.
Near-term spreads are expected to remain in contango well into June as the Asian market is expected to be oversupplied for at least one more month due to cargoes from the West, traders said.
Fuel oil dealers said Indonesia's state-owned oil concern Pertamina is expected to allocate 3.1 million barrels of low sulphur waxy residue (LSWR) for June, compared to 3.9 million barrels for May.
Any bullish effects from the smaller allocation, however, will be counterbalanced by sluggish buying interest from Japan, they said. --Tokyo Energy Desk +81-3-3432-8837
